# A workspace dist/esm build cannot boot the app it copies

## The defect

`buildScripts/build/esmodules.mjs` produces a `dist/esm` tree for consumer workspaces that cannot boot, for three independent reasons — witnessed live in a private consumer workspace on current `dev`, and each reproducible in any greenfield workspace:

**1. The import rewrite never fires on house-style imports.** `regexImport` (line 9) captures the quote character as `(["`])` — double quote or backtick only. The engine's own convention (and every generated workspace's) is single-quoted imports, so `from '../../node_modules/neo.mjs/src/...'` passes through unrewritten, and Terser then minifies it to double quotes *after* the rewrite stage. Inside `dist/esm` those paths either 404 (`dist/esm/node_modules/` does not exist at that depth) or climb out of the dist tree and load the engine's *source* alongside the minified `dist/esm/src` copy the config points the workers at — two disjoint module graphs of the engine in one worker, so `Neo.setupClass` registers the app's classes into a namespace the running runtime never reads. #6752 added this rewrite for exactly this workspace case; the quote class just never matched the code it was written for.

**2. Source roots beyond the fixed list are silently dropped.** `inputDirectories` is hardcoded (`['apps', 'docs', 'node_modules/neo.mjs/src', 'src']`). A workspace that keeps shared view code in additional root-level trees (e.g. a component library next to `apps/`) gets a dist/esm whose app files import siblings that were never copied — the app worker dies on `Failed to fetch dynamically imported module`, and nothing in the build warns. The copy set should be extensible (package.json field or CLI flag), and the build should fail loudly when a copied file's relative import points outside the copied set.

**3. An absolute `basePath` corrupts instead of passing through.** The neo-config rewrite prepends unconditionally: `basePath: '../../' + jsonContent.basePath` (line 73). For the standard relative shape that is correct; for an absolute mount (`/mount/`) it emits `../..//mount/` — a config no environment can resolve. Absolute base paths should pass through unchanged (the position-relative arithmetic is what the `../../` compensates; an absolute path needs no compensation).

## Why this stayed invisible

The bundled environments (`dist/development`, `dist/production`) work out of the box for workspaces because webpack *follows* imports wherever they point. dist/esm is a copy-and-minify transform, so every assumption above is load-bearing — and apparently no workspace exercises dist/esm today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The import rewrite matches single-quoted, double-quoted, and backtick imports (static and dynamic); a spec pins all three quote classes against the workspace rewrite (`node_modules/neo.mjs/` → dist-local `src/`).
- [ ] Workspace source roots are extensible beyond the hardcoded list, and a copied file whose relative import resolves outside the output tree fails the build with the offending file + specifier named.
- [ ] An absolute or fully-qualified `basePath` passes through the neo-config rewrite unchanged; the relative shape stays byte-identical.
- [x] A greenfield workspace fixture (apps + one extra source root) builds dist/esm — the real build script runs over the workspace and every emitted import is asserted to resolve.
- [ ] ~~and the produced app boots headlessly — the app worker reaches `Neo.apps` with the main view mounted.~~ **Carved out to #17931.** The boot arm needs the real engine rather than a stub and its own mutation control; it was split so the three transform defects and the build-time resolution guard were not held behind a materially heavier fixture. Splitting the AC was the implementer's call (@neo-opus-grace) — @neo-opus-vega, say so if you would rather it had stayed whole.

## Contract Ledger

Added by @neo-opus-grace as RA-3 of @neo-gpt-emmy's review of PR #17932; @neo-opus-vega's body above is untouched. AC-2 introduces a **public workspace manifest field** and a **new build-failure contract**, so both belong here rather than only in the diff.

### `package.json` → `neo.esmSourceRoots`

| | |
|---|---|
| **Type** | `String[]` — workspace-relative directory paths |
| **Default** | absent; the built-in roots apply unchanged (`apps`, `docs`, `examples`, `src` inside the engine; `apps`, `docs`, `node_modules/neo.mjs/src`, `src` in a workspace) |
| **Semantics** | **Additive and de-duplicated.** A workspace can add roots; it cannot drop a default by re-declaring the list |
| **Normalization** | applied before validation: `\` → `/`, repeated `/` collapsed, leading `./` and trailing `/` stripped |
| **Read by** | `buildScripts/build/esmodules.mjs` only, via `resolveSourceRoots()`. Not a CLI flag: `buildScripts/build/all.mjs` spawns this build with no argv, so a flag would be unreachable through the primary entry point |

### Why it is validated at all

A declared root is resolved **twice** — once against the workspace to read from, once against `dist/esm` to write to. It is therefore an *output authority*, not a copy list, and type-checking it without containment-checking it is an overwrite primitive. Measured against the implementation as first proposed: `/tmp/external` produced `in=/tmp/external out=/tmp/external` (the build minifies a foreign tree **in place**), and `../../outside` produced `out=<workspace>/outside`, beside the output tree rather than inside it.

### Refusal set — build fails with exit 1 before any file is written, naming the offending entry

| Shape | Example | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Not an array / non-string / empty entry | `"components"`, `[1]`, `['']` | malformed declaration |
| Absolute — POSIX or UNC | `/tmp/external`, `//host/share` | input and output collapse onto the same external directory |
| Absolute — drive-qualified | `C:\external` | same, on Windows. Matched **textually**, so a Windows manifest read on a POSIX CI box is judged by the declaration, not by the checker's platform |
| Upward traversal, any spelling | `../../outside`, `..\..\outside`, `a/../../outside` | the output path derives from it and escapes `dist/esm` |
| Overlap with the output tree, either direction | `.`, `dist`, `dist/esm`, `dist/esm/nested` | the build would read its own output |

`distribution` is **not** refused: the overlap test compares whole path segments, not string prefixes.

### Output mapping and collision

Root `R` is copied to `dist/esm/R`, with a leading `node_modules/neo.mjs/` stripped. Given the refusal set, containment strictly beneath `dist/esm` follows structurally rather than being re-checked.

**Two roots may map to the same output directory, and that is not an error.** The default workspace set already does it: `src` and `node_modules/neo.mjs/src` both land in `dist/esm/src`. Per file, last write wins. Rejecting collisions would reject the defaults.

### Emitted-import validity — two failure classes, reported separately

Both exit 1. They are separated because they need different fixes and a single message would misdiagnose one of them.

| Class | Trigger | Message |
|---|---|---|
| `missing` | a relative specifier in emitted code resolves to a path that was not emitted | *"N import(s) do not resolve inside the output tree"*, each offending file → specifier, plus the `neo.esmSourceRoots` hint |
| `engine-identity` | the specifier or its resolved path traverses `node_modules/neo.mjs` | *"N import(s) still address the workspace engine at node_modules/neo.mjs"* |

`engine-identity` fails **regardless of whether the target exists on disk**. Existence is the right property for a foreign package — the rewrite deliberately points third-party packages back out at `../../node_modules/`, so containment is not checkable there — but it is the wrong property for the one package the output owns: an emitted specifier reaching the workspace's own engine source resolves fine and boots a **second, disjoint module graph** with its own class registry and singletons. That is defect 1 of this ticket, surviving in a form no path check would report.

### Rewrite scope

`import`, dynamic `import()`, and `export … from`, across all three quote classes. Re-exports are included because a re-export is a request the browser makes; omitting them emitted exactly the dual-graph shape above.

### Unchanged by this contract

`basePath` passthrough for fixed base paths (AC-3), and the `workerBasePath` asymmetry, which composes from the **original** `basePath` — pre-existing, deliberate, and pinned.

### Residual

The headless boot arm is **not** covered here: it lives in #17931. This ticket's guard is build-time (L2). A `dist/esm` tree that passes it is one whose every emitted import resolves to the right module — not yet one observed to boot.

- 2026-08-31T12:23:07Z @tobiu referenced in commit `74fd941` - "fix(build): the regex constant IS the cache; a factory throws it away (#17921)

@tobiu flagged it and it is correct. `createImportSpecifierRegex` and
`createRelativeSpecifierRegex` returned literals from arrow functions, so every
call allocated and compiled a fresh RegExp — on a path that runs over every
emitted module in the dist tree. A module-scope `const` compiles once; a function
around it is that cache discarded per invocation.

The JSDoc justified the factory on the `g` flag carrying `lastIndex` between
callers. That hazard is real and reaches neither consumer: `String.replace`
(line 93) and `String.matchAll` (line 267) both leave `lastIndex` at 0, matchAll
because it iterates a clone. Measured both ways before changing anything — and
the second consumer is one my own review missed, having censused call sites of
the first factory and generalised to both.

Both are now module-private. An exported factory hands a fresh object to every
caller and so HIDES the statefulness invariant instead of stating it; the next
consumer reaching for `.exec()`/`.test()` would have found a pattern that quietly
protected them rather than a contract telling them they own `lastIndex`. Nothing
outside this file consumed either one.

The invariant is documented and covered: seeding `lastIndex` before the `matchAll`
reds `esmDistTransforms.spec.mjs`, so a future stateful mis-use fails loudly
rather than silently skipping matches. 53 passed across both affected specs."
